A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TEGA study and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–I. No material gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original transformer and TEGA experiments on three knowledge graphs, including benchmark results, ablations, and additional analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 2–8 and the architecture, efficiency, depth, and pooling comparisons in the appendices.

M1.justification: Section 6 retains the same TEGA architecture, LogiRPE attention equations, and free-variable pooling procedure. The training objective and inference procedure are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use FB15k, FB15k-237, and NELL995 with the same 23 seen and 32 unseen query types. The syntax-comparison subset and query-reversion scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains BetaE, ConE, CQD, LMPNN, SQE-LSTM, and the same four positional-encoding variants. Comparator membership in the inductive-bias, TEGA, and appendix architecture comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendices A, G, and I retain the same query counts, graph splits, MRR evaluation, training budgets, and model configurations. No experimental protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The syntax, permutation, embedding, and inductive-bias analyses remain unchanged, as do the TEGA ablations and attention visualization. Appendices H–I retain the same architecture, depth, and pooling analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical values and result entries are unchanged, but Table 15 corrects highlighted rankings. For NELL995, bold emphasis moves from encoder-decoder scores 48.7 and 55.7 to the higher encoder-only Relative PE scores 49.8 and 57.4 for OOD(Q)/ID(K) and all-query ID(K), respectively. This corrects ranking indications rather than reporting new performance.

T1.justification: The logical definitions, distribution-shift formulation, attention equations, query-graph definition, and evaluation mathematics are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The benchmark, architectural investigation, and TEGA contributions retain the same scope and claims. The conclusion's replacement of 'ability to perform complex logical inference' with 'logical entailment ability' restates the existing claim.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations and interpretations are retained. Limitations concerning single free variables, explicit token labeling, unseen logical operators, and scalability remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The code/data access statement and Appendix I are unchanged, including four A100 GPUs, two-day training, batch size 1024, 400-dimensional embeddings, learning rate 0.0001, and implementation details.

R1.justification: Section 7 adds AutoSchemaKG (Bai et al., 2025a) to the existing discussion of natural-language query settings. The retitled KnowShiftQA reference retains arXiv identifier 2412.08985 and is the same previously cited work. Research positioning otherwise remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract shortens 'the reasoning capability of transformers' to 'their reasoning capability,' and the conclusion similarly condenses its final sentence. Bibliographic titles and year labels are updated; section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: Table 15 revises bold and underlined emphasis, correcting best-score, tie, and runner-up markings. Wording and bibliography edits cause limited text reflow. Figures, table structures, and their placement are otherwise unchanged.

improvement.justification: Table 15 becomes more accurate to read: v2 incorrectly bolds lower NELL995 encoder-decoder scores, while v3 correctly highlights the higher encoder-only Relative PE scores and fixes other ranking marks. This resolves a limited presentation error. The wording and citation edits are modest, and the methods, numerical evidence, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
